question: Can a model selected by cross-validated search over SVM, LightGBM and a soft-voting ensemble give more accurate music-emotion suggestions than a standard random forest on a public music-audio feature dataset?
method: Stratified 80/20 split (seed 42); preprocessing fitted on train only. Baseline: random forest with default settings. Improved: candidate models (RBF SVM with balanced class weights and Platt probabilities, soft-voting ensemble of SVM + balanced RF + balanced LightGBM, balanced LightGBM grid) compared by 5-fold stratified CV macro-F1 on the training split only; the best is refit with seeds 42, 43, 44 and the test set is used once per model.
baseline: Standard RandomForestClassifier with default settings (generic suggestion model).
improved: Selected by training-set CV: ensemble with params {'C': 10}, class-balanced, standardised inside a pipeline.
notes: Selected configuration: ensemble {'C': 10} (train CV macro-F1 0.8000). Single stratified split, so the test set is small (about 80 songs) and differences are noisy; the three seeds capture model randomness only, not split variability. The test set was not used for any selection. Brier score is a calibration proxy, not a user-trust measurement. This is a stand-in experiment; the motivating paper's model and results are not stated and are not reproduced. The ucimlrepo import of dataset 862 is refused by the service, so the script falls back to downloading the same official UCI zip directly; the data content is identical.
